We need to solve the equation $Ax=0.$ First, we find the row echelon form of $A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & 9 \\ 4 & 9 & 8 \\ 4 & 8 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 9 & 8 \\ 4 & 8 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 \\ 4 & 8 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{2}-4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$, and we have one free variables, ${x}_{3}.$ That means we need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ in terms of ${x}_{3}.$

From the second equation we get ${x}_{2}=4{x}_{3}.$ Substituting ${x}_{2}=4{x}_{3}$ into the first equation, we get 

$$
{x}_{1}+2(4{x}_{3})+3{x}_{3}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-11{x}_{3}.
$$

So the set of all the solutions of $Ax=0$ is

$$
\text{Null}(A)={[\begin{aligned}-11{x}_{3} \\ 4{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{3}\in R}.
$$
